soil_type: Expansive Victoria clay — USDA SSURGO maps 58% of Nueces County to Victoria clay (0–1% slopes), very-high shrink-swell; tidal-flats fine sand near the bays and on Padre Island.
soil_leak_note: Victoria clay (linear extensibility up to 18.7%, up to 61% clay) swells with rain and shrinks hard in drought, cycling slabs and snapping buried line joints; with only ~31.7 in of rain a year the wet-dry swing is sharp — long dry spells shrink clay away from slabs, then September deluges swell it back. Salt in coastal soil also works on concrete and metal pipe, and a high water table in low ground keeps buried lines wet.
foundation_types: Slab-on-grade dominates (standard for post-1960s Coastal Bend builds); pier-and-beam in pre-1960s central-city homes; elevated/piling foundations on North Padre Island and waterfront lots.
housing_era: Full range: 1940s–60s central city (Downtown, Bay Area); 1970s–90s Southside build-out; 2000s+ new construction on the Southside (King's Crossing, The Lakes) and North Padre Island. Median year built ~1980.
common_pipe_materials: Pre-1980s central-city homes: galvanized steel and cast iron; 1980s–90s: copper and PVC; 2000s+: PEX and PVC; salt-air corrosion accelerates failure of exposed metal pipe and fittings.
neighborhoods: Downtown, Calallen, Flour Bluff, Southside, North Padre Island, Ocean Drive, Lamar Park, Annaville
